thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Smart-routing fallback loop detected. Starting 08:03 UTC — sudden spike in fallback traffic to eu-west-1 and us-central-1; error-rate up 7x, p95 latency > 3s, some clients receiving model-mismatch errors. Autoremote fallback activated (policy v3.2.1).

pagerbot: Paging @amelia (oncall) and @rachel-sre. Escalation to SRE lead if not ack in 3m.

amenia: ack — investigating. Pulling routing dashboard and recent policy changes.

rachel-sre: I'm on it, taking pager. Quick summary from me: traffic routing started failing over customers into eu-west-1 at 08:02; capacity there is healthy but model variant landing there is a quantized tiny model that doesn't accept float-embedding payloads -> 400/422 for some clients. Clients retry aggressively (backoff=0s for some SDK versions) and we see amplified load.

dave-infra: Confirming region capacity ok. I see repeated new sessions from same client IPs causing KV cache churn. Also some autoscale triggers in eu-west-1 due to increased connections.

liu-ml: Noting that recent routing-polciy change (rollout at 07:58) included a fallback rule: `fallback_variant: "small-quant"` for cost tiering. That was intended for cold-start low-priority traffic but is now being applied to production requests because of a tag mismatch (tag: "tier:unknown").

amelia: can you paste the policy snippet?

liu-ml: Sure — pasted below:

```
route {
  match: region == "global" && client.tier != "enterprise"
  primary: model-v2.1
  fallback: small-quant
  fallback_policy: auto
}
```

liu-ml: The bug is fallback_policy:auto combined with smart-routing's 'compatible-variant' logic — it chose small-quant even though the request payload requires float embeddings.

josh-prod: Customer impact check: I see three paying customers with elevated 5xxs (acme-corp, beeline-ai, studyapp). Support tickets started at 08:05. Emma, can you triage comms?

emma-se: On it. Drafting status update. Short term - asking affected customers to disable client-side immediate retries (sdk v0.9 has broken backoff). Also offering temporary bypass to dedicated capacity if needed.

rachel-sre: Mitigation plan (short-term):
1) Disable auto fallback for routing policy group -> set fallback_policy: reject for policy v3.2.1 (prevents silent variant mismatch).
2) Push a targeted killswitch to reject requests that would be routed to small-quant for embedding payloads (pattern match on content-type / embedding flag).
3) Throttle retries at the edge for X-Client-SDK versions <= 0.9.
4) Contact top customers with recommended SDK patch.

amelia: executing step 1 now. Command: `rkctl routing update --policy-id v3.2.1 --set fallback_policy=reject`

(dave-infra reacts :white_check_mark:)

amelia: update applied. policy v3.2.1 fallback_policy=reject — confirmed via `/api/v1/routing/policies/v3.2.1` shows fallback_policy: "reject".

incident-bot: System note: routing policy update broadcasted to all edge clusters.

rachel-sre: Step 2 — deploying a short circuit rule on the edge: `if (requested_model_variant == "small-quant" && payload.type == "embedding") -> 409` to avoid wrong-model attempts.

liu-ml: Pushing variant compatibility check hotfix to edge validators to reject incompatible payloads.

josh-prod: Emma - send status note to support with times, affected customers, mitigation steps. Include workaround for disabling immediate retries and instructions to enable dedicated path.

emma-se: Drafted: "We're seeing elevated error rates caused by a routing fallback to a reduced-precision variant. We've disabled automatic fallback and will throttle retry traffic at the edge. If you see repeated 4xx/5xx, please update SDK to v0.9.2 or contact us for a dedicated route." Sending now.

dave-infra: Observability note — we need to keep an eye for thundering herd patterns from the same client IPs. I've added temporary connection-level rate limits (20 req/s per client IP) at the LB to damp retries.

amelia: LB throttles in place. Monitoring effects. p95 latency falling from 3.4s -> 1.2s over next 6m. Error-rate dropping but still above baseline.

rachel-sre: On-call handoff: @amelia you'll keep watch for next 30m, then hand to @rachel-sre for postmortem and service restoration validation. If error-rate doesn't fall below 2x baseline by 09:15 UTC escalate to infra lead.

amelia: ack, I'll stay on for 30m and gather logs for postmortem.

liu-ml: Note for postmortem — root cause = routing policy tag-mismatch + permissive fallback_policy:auto + some SDKs with aggressive retry/backoff=0. Combined created a feedback loop where failing requests were retried and routed to the wrong variant, which then rejected them and retriggers failover.

josh-prod: Customer impact summary for the incident page: ~3 enterprise customers affected for ~22 minutes, broader 5xx spike impacting ~1.8% of requests for 12m. We'll propose corrective actions: stricter compatibility checks, default fallback_policy=reject, SDK backoff enforcement, and routing policy rollout gating.

emma-se: Customers notified, some accepted temporary dedicated capacity. Support triage open.

rachel-sre: Post-incident actions (short list):
- Hotfix: edge validator to reject incompatible variants (deployed).
- Policy change: default fallback -> reject (PR open).
- Telemetry: add metric for "variant_incompat_retries" and alert at 0.1% of requests.
- SDK: release v0.9.2 that enforces exponential backoff by default.

amelia: Logging bundle for postmortem uploaded to #incidents-artifacts: s3://redwood-incidents/2280012345/logs.tar.gz

pagerbot: Reminder: create postmortem doc in 24h and assign owners.

rachel-sre: I'll own the postmortem, assigning liu-ml (root cause), dave-infra (scale & LB changes), josh-prod (customer comms), emma-se (support), amelia (oncall timeline).

amelia: Noted. Closing on-call shift in 30m once metrics stabilize.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (09:03 UTC). Final metrics: error spike resolved after throttles + policy update; 22m duration; mitigations applied and follow-ups scheduled.

josh-prod: Thanks team. We'll include a short blameless summary for execs and affected customers.

emma-se: I'll coordinate customer follow-ups tomorrow morning PST.

rachel-sre: Postmortem draft expected in 48h.

(reacts: :thumbsup: from several people)
